title: Review without losing the page
excerpt: A practical way to keep product context attached to every piece of feedback.

sections.heading: The page is part of the feedback
paragraphs: Screenshots capture pixels, but they lose routes, responsive state, component boundaries, and the exact DOM element that needs attention.
fivepixels keeps that context on the staging interface so a reviewer can point, explain, and return to the same place later.

sections.heading: A smaller review loop
paragraphs: Start on one high-value screen, agree on what ready for review means, and resolve every marker before expanding the workflow.
items: Leave feedback on the real element.
Recheck and resolve in the same context.

title: A one-page rollout beats a company-wide launch
excerpt: How to introduce interface feedback without changing every team ritual at once.

sections.heading: Choose a page with real review traffic
paragraphs: A checkout, onboarding flow, or internal dashboard gives the team enough real feedback to learn the workflow without creating a process migration project.

sections.heading: Measure clarity, not activity
paragraphs: The useful signal is whether developers understand the requested change on the first read and whether reviewers can verify it without rebuilding context.

title: Markers that survive UI change
excerpt: Why DOM-aware anchors are more useful than coordinates when an interface keeps moving.

sections.heading: Coordinates are temporary
paragraphs: A pixel coordinate describes a viewport at one moment. A DOM-aware marker can describe the element, nearby structure, and the route where feedback was created.

sections.heading: Use stable intent where it matters
paragraphs: Add explicit report identifiers only to critical or repeated surfaces. Let automatic matching handle the rest so instrumentation stays lightweight.

title: The first fivepixels note
excerpt: What we are building and why staging review deserves a purpose-built layer.

sections.heading: Feedback belongs on the interface
paragraphs: fivepixels is an open-source React review layer for teams that already have a staging environment but still coordinate visual feedback through screenshots and chat.
